regime.skew: near-flat at +0.40, the thinnest protection bid of the series (+2.90 on 2026-09-02)
regime.label: Dealer long-gamma cage holds 1070-1100 at a series-low 12.21% IV, with the first put-side unwind print
evidence: Net GEX +11,138 index-point units is the second-highest print of the U26 series and 56x the +199 of 2026-09-03; strike-level GEX peaks at 1100/+4,700 and 1080/+3,572, so dealers are longest gamma exactly where price is trading.

Realised range is running at 38% of implied: the last four sessions closed 1079.4, 1083.3, 1081.9 and 1082.4 - a 3.9-point spread and a 3.18-point average daily move against an 8.33-point 1-sigma day. That gap is the long-gamma dampener working.

1090 gamma flip has been fixed for four straight sessions and sits 7.6 points above spot 1082.4, inside one 1-sigma day; cumulative GEX is still -345 at 1080 and +2,400 at 1090, so the cage lid is one ordinary session away.

12.21% ATM IV is a new series low (12.44% yesterday, 14.09% on 2026-09-03) and put OI fell 231 to 44,058 - the first and largest put-side decline in the eight-session window, an early unwind flag rather than a regime change.

S50U26.today_summary: 1082.4 closed 0.5 points higher and 12.4 points - 1.5 sigma - above the 1070 max pain that has now been parked for five straight sessions. 0.97 put/call volume is the first sub-parity print since 2026-09-04 and comes off a 46% collapse in put volume, 2,659 to 1,434, while 1,473 call lots held steady. The live near-money structure is 2,804 call OI at 1100 on 235 lots against 1,953 put OI at 1050 on 156 lots, with the heaviest volume at 1080/271 calls and 1060/387 puts - flow is concentrated inside the cage, not at its edges. The 16,321-contract 910 put wall again fails the Vol2Vol filter on 5 lots, zero gamma and a stale 35.5% IV, so it carries no hedging force.
what_changed: Put volume halved, 2,659 to 1,434 lots, dragging the P/C volume ratio from 1.50 to 0.97 - the first session since 2026-09-04 where puts did not lead the tape.

Put OI fell 231 to 44,058, the first decline of the window, led by 1050 shedding 211 contracts while 1000 added 126 - protection rolled down and away from the near-money strike rather than being added.
ATM IV compressed another 0.23 points to a series-low 12.21%, cutting the 1-sigma day to 8.33 from 8.48 and from 9.39 on 2026-09-03.
25-delta skew flattened again to +0.40 from +0.78, extending a run from +2.90 on 2026-09-02; the downside-insurance bid has drained even as put OI stays 2.27x calls.
S50U26.five_day_thesis: Five sessions ago, on 2026-09-04, the future was 1062.3 with net GEX at just +1,188 and the gamma flip 47.7 points overhead at 1110; the 20.1-point rally to 1082.4 since then has been absorbed rather than chased, with dealers getting 9.4x longer gamma on the way up and the flip migrating down to 1090. Max pain drifted only 1060 to 1070 against that 20.1-point move and the 1100 call wall never budged, adding 156 contracts to 2,804 - the structure let price come to it instead of moving with it. IV compressed 0.90 points over the same stretch, 13.11% to 12.21%, which is the signature of dealers being paid to fade excursions rather than of a market pricing a catalyst. Put OI still grew +1,989 to 44,058 over the five sessions, but 25-delta skew halved from +1.05 to +0.40 - this is calendar collar and covered-call mechanics parking hedges on the burden map, not a directional vote, and today's 231-contract put unwind is the first crack in that build. The cage is therefore 1070 to 1100 with 12 trading sessions left to the 2026-09-29 expiry: 1070 is where strike-level GEX changes sign and 1100 is where 2,804 contracts of call OI sit, and nothing in the last five sessions has closed outside it.

strategies.name: Iron condor 1030P / 1050P x 1100C / 1120C
strategies.rationale: Sells both live near-money walls - 1,953 put OI at 1050 and 2,804 call OI at 1100 - outside a +11,138 net-GEX cage where realised movement has been running at 38% of the 8.33-point implied 1-sigma day. This is the long-gamma / Pinning / compressed-IV cell of the matrix: neutral direction, short volatility, defined risk.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point wing width minus about 5.50 points of net credit at mid = roughly 14.50 points per side; both sides cannot lose at once.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close beyond 1100 or below 1050 - either breach puts price outside the strikes the cage is built on.

strategies.name: Put credit spread 1060 / 1040
strategies.rationale: Spot 1082.4 sits above the 1070 pin, which is the matrix row calling for a credit spread leaning toward the anchor: it sells the 25-delta strike at 1060 and buys the 10-delta at 1040, both below the 1070 GEX sign flip. The 2.55-point credit against 17.45 points of risk is itself the read - 12.21% IV pays very little for range, so this expresses the pin rather than harvesting premium.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point width minus about 2.55 points of net credit at mid = roughly 17.45 points.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close below 1070, where strike-level net GEX turns negative and dealer hedging stops dampening the move.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1070 / 1050
strategies.rationale: The tail the two short-vol structures above do not cover: below 1070 cumulative GEX is negative all the way down and the next live put OI is only 1,323 at 1040, so dealer hedging flips from fading the move to feeding it. At 11.83% IV on the 1070 put - a series low - this buys that convexity for 3.7 points, and today's 231-contract put unwind is the first evidence the hedging bid holding the cage together can thin out.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = about 3.70 points of net debit at mid; max value 20 points at or below 1050.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close back above 1090, the gamma flip, which restores the long-gamma dampener the structure is designed to trade against.

S50U26.prediction: Base case is continued 1070-1100 containment while net GEX holds above +10,000, with 1082.4 leaning back toward the 1070 anchor on any excursion larger than the 8.33-point 1-sigma day and upside capped near the 2,804-contract 1100 wall; the 3.18-point average daily move of the last four sessions is the realistic range, not the implied one. That bias breaks on a daily close below 1070, where strike-level GEX goes negative into strikes carrying only 1,323-1,390 puts, or on a close above 1090 that holds with 1100 call OI being bought rather than sold - the first would be a squeeze lower, the second the cage failing upward. The signal to watch for the second consecutive session is the put side: a further decline in the 44,058 put OI alongside sub-1.0 put/call volume would shift this from Pinning toward Unwind and remove the mechanical support under the range.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and no execution is being recommended. SET50 options are European and cash-settled on the SET50 index, so there is no physical share delivery to force stock-side hedging into strikes; the 1070 max-pain magnet is a statistical tendency and is structurally weaker here than for physically-settled single stocks, and macro or news flow can override the option structure outright. Defined-risk is not low-risk: the condor above carries a real 14.50-point max loss per side and the 1060/1040 credit spread risks 17.45 points to collect 2.55, a negative-skew payoff of many small gains and occasional large ones - survival comes from size, not from being right. The 16,321-contract 910 put wall fails the Vol2Vol filter (5 lots, zero gamma, stale 35.5% IV) and must not be read as support. All figures derive from the 2026-09-11T02:00:09+07:00 scrape of a 25-row chain; 12 trading sessions remain to the 2026-09-29 last trading date.
